column1: Unlike the analysis of the closed economy, the Obstfeld-Rogo¤ model implies that monetary-induced output movements would have persistent real e¤ects by altering the distribution of wealth between economies. In general, standard open-economy frameworks used for policy analysis assume that the real e¤ects of monetary policy arise only in the short run and are due to nominal rigidities. Over time, as wages and prices adjust, real output, real interest rates, and the real exchange rate return to equilibrium levels that are independent of monetary policy. This long-run neutrality means that these models, like their closed-economy counterparts, imply that the longrun e¤ects of monetary policy fall on prices, inflation, nominal interest rates, and the nominal exchange rate. In the short run, however, monetary policy can have important e¤ects on the manner in which real output and the real exchange rate fluctuate around their longer-run equilibrium values.
